solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A cent tip, perhaps? Definitely!

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether leaving a single cent as a tip counts as meagre, and is assured it does.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'perhaps' rearranges A CENT TIP, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a one-cent tip is certainly a measly sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny, insultingly small payment such as a one-cent gratuity is a classic example of a meagre amount.

clue.text: Mean to snoop around a junior officer

indicators.note: around means the snooping word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: to pry is to snoop
Lt is short for lieutenant, a junior officer

explanation.surface: It is mean to spy on a lowly officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb (intend), but it is the adjective meaning stingy or meagre.
explanation.definitionFit: A paltry sum is a mean, meagre one: both words mean miserably small.

clue.text: Practically free at a pound per thousand

definitions.text: Practically free at a pound per thousand

parts.words: Practically free at a pound per thousand
parts.note: a pound for a thousand items works out at ten per old penny, almost nothing each

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something so plentiful it is almost worthless literally names ten items for one penny, and a thousand for a pound matches that rate.

clue.text: Part of theatre I shall briefly mention

indicators.note: mention means the contraction is said aloud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: I shall shortened is the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: I will quickly say something about a section of a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage between rows of seats is one part of a theatre's auditorium.

clue.text: Various sources supply this wealthy ruler

indicators.note: various means in differing forms, so these letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Several sources provide information on a rich king.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient king of Lydia was proverbially the richest man alive, hence 'as rich as' him.

clue.text: Censorship?

parts.note: split it as censor plus ship: a censor cuts material, and a small fast sailing vessel bears the same name

explanation.walkthrough: Read the one word as 'censor ship': a ship that is also one who cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor removes scenes and lines, so the person doing it is literally one who snips things out; the question mark flags this playful sense.

clue.text: A French tree with uniform heart, unlike 27

definitions.note: 27 is IN FAVOUR, so its opposite is disliked

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: heart means the letter goes into the very middle of the tree word

parts.note: a poplar is a tree
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A tree in France with a uniform core stands out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 27 across, IN FAVOUR; the opposite of being favoured is being disliked.
explanation.definitionFit: Not being well liked is the reverse of being looked upon kindly, an antonym of the linked entry.

clue.text: One has a crack in this German city

definitions.meaning: one who has a crack, a go, at something is a person who attempts it
an ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has a go at things is one who tries, and the same spelling names an old Roman city on the Moselle.

clue.text: Trains ensure it when travelling

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Railway services make sure of it on journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' suggests railways, but it means groups of attendants following a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can mean a body of followers accompanying an important person, the same as an entourage.

clue.text: Goal from fifty yards? It's not very likely

definitions.meaning: a strike attempted from a great distance, as in football
an outside chance, a bet unlikely to come off

explanation.definitionFit: A strike from far away is literally a distant attempt, and figuratively the phrase means an improbable outcome.

clue.text: Second run off is needed in this race

parts.note: to run off copies is to print them

explanation.surface: An athlete needs a second attempt after a false start in this race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off' suggests a deciding re-run of a race, but here it means producing printed copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a short flat-out race, the kind run at top speed over a short distance.

clue.text: Caterpillar food, commonly

definitions.meaning: an insect larva, such as a caterpillar

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an insect larva and, informally, something to eat.

clue.text: Anna was once part of it in India

definitions.text: Anna was once part of it in India

parts.words: Anna was once part of it in India
parts.note: the anna was an old Indian coin worth one sixteenth of the main currency unit

explanation.definitionFit: Before decimalisation, India's currency unit was divided into sixteen annas, so the anna was a fraction of it.

clue.text: Dispute with press could be a load of rubbish

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or quarrel
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Arguing with the newspapers could turn out to be worthless nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' reads as the newspapers, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes; 'a load of rubbish' is literal discarded metal, not nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal sold for recycling is literally waste material, a heap of junk.

clue.text: A sound heard from bugs

indicators.note: heard says the words are taken as spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sound is a noise, giving the phrase 'a noise'

explanation.surface: A noise is picked up from listening devices or insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' suggests insects or hidden microphones, but it is the verb meaning irritates.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or bother them, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Orthodox old bishop needs help

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a help is a domestic worker, a servant

explanation.surface: A traditionalist elderly cleric requires assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone orthodox in religion follows the rules and customs carefully, keeping all the observances.

clue.text: Mostly brave and quiet, that's difficult to deal with

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: bold means brave
sh is the call for quiet
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Someone who is largely brave and silent proves hard to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroppy, uncooperative person is described in British slang this way, from the Bolsheviks.

clue.text: A stroke of luck, of course!

definitions.text: A stroke of luck, of course!

parts.words: A stroke of luck, of course!
parts.note: a golf shot that drops straight in from the tee: a single lucky stroke on a golf course

explanation.definitionFit: A tee shot that drops straight into the cup is a single fortunate stroke made on a golf course.

clue.text: It may also be applied to flannel

definitions.text: It may also be applied to flannel

parts.words: It may also be applied to flannel
parts.note: flannel is both a washcloth and smooth flattering talk

explanation.definitionFit: Liquid cleanser for a washcloth shares its name with flattery, which is what 'flannel' also means in British slang.

clue.text: First postwar travel adventures

parts.note: Homer's epic of Odysseus wandering home after the Trojan War is the first great tale of postwar travel

explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic follows Odysseus on his long voyage home after the Trojan War, so it is the original after-the-war journey story.

clue.text: Income in Shanghai you earn regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: What you take home in a Chinese city you get steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese currency unit is what earnings in Shanghai are counted in.

clue.text: Iron law used as punishment

definitions.note: a phrase describing an object, here standing for the cane itself

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a rule is a law

explanation.surface: A strict regulation on metal is enforced as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler or cane formerly used by schoolmasters for striking pupils is an instrument of chastisement.

clue.text: Fabric woven from finest end of cloth

indicators.note: woven suggests strands interlaced into a new pattern, so these letters are rearranged
end of means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A material is made from the best part of a roll of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woven' rearranges FINEST together with H, the last letter of 'cloth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Open mesh material, as used for stockings, is a type of textile.

clue.text: Mountain range referred to by letter

definitions.meaning: a Spanish word for a jagged chain of mountains
the NATO phonetic code word for the letter S

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a jagged mountain chain and is the radio code word for one letter.

clue.text: Inland waters where her boats are deployed by day

indicators.note: deployed means set out in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lake district where her boats are put out on the water during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'are deployed' shuffles HERBOATS together with D (day) into a single run.
explanation.definitionFit: This Norfolk network of rivers and lakes, popular for boating holidays in eastern England, is a body of inland waterways.

clue.text: Competition in sport never rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A contest in a sport that was never turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A single contest in a sports programme, such as a race, is a competition.

clue.text: First person to back a liberal defence

indicators.note: to back means coming at the back, after the other pieces

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: The first individual to support a liberal politician offers a justification.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse showing one was elsewhere when a crime happened is a plea used in one's legal defence.

clue.text: Cast down from a pedestal

parts.note: a base is the pedestal a statue stands on

explanation.surface: Thrown from a plinth, a statue falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests casting a statue, but 'Cast down' means humiliate.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble or degrade someone is to bring them low, to lower them in dignity.

clue.text: No dispute over billing in such a show

definitions.text: No dispute over billing in such a show

parts.words: No dispute over billing in such a show
parts.note: billing is the order of performers' names on a poster; with a single performer there is nothing to argue over

explanation.definitionFit: A solo performance has only one star, so nobody can quarrel about whose name tops the poster.

clue.text: What persona grata would be for

definitions.text: What persona grata would be for

parts.words: What persona grata would be for
parts.note: a persona grata is a welcome, approved person, one who is liked and accepted

explanation.definitionFit: Being welcome and approved of means being looked on with approval, the state of being liked.

clue.text: Staple hard to handle when hot

definitions.text: Staple hard to handle when hot

parts.words: Staple hard to handle when hot
parts.note: a staple food that, as the idiom 'hot ...' says, is a tricky issue no one wants to hold

explanation.definitionFit: This tuber is a dietary staple, and the idiom of a hot one means a controversial issue that is hard to handle.

clue.text: Unmentioned extras for Caesar?

parts.note: the Latin phrase meaning 'and the rest' covers further items not named, and Caesar spoke Latin

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for 'and the rest' stands for further items left unlisted, and Caesar would have said it in his own tongue.
